transcript.content: Hello, please have a seat. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because... well, I've been doing some things lately that don't really make sense. Mostly at work and school. Like, I'm a bookkeeping clerk, and I've started lining up all the receipts across the floor instead of filing them. And I'll tap the calculator in sets of nine before I can use it. Or I'll just stand by the copier with my hands held up in the air, and I don't move until someone comes over and asks if I'm okay. It's just... I know it's weird, but I keep doing it.
What goes through your mind right before or while you are doing these things?

Well, it's hard to describe exactly. My mind just gets really crowded and jumps around a lot. Like, if I'm trying to explain to someone why a ledger is off at work, my thoughts will just... jump from my tuition deadlines to tax rules, and then suddenly I'm thinking about studio lighting and number patterns. I try to explain it out loud, but people tell me they cannot follow how I got from one point to the next. It all makes sense to me in the moment, but my thoughts just won't stay in a straight line.

He'll say things like, 'check line seven' or 'you missed the sign.' It sounds so clear that I actually stop and look around, but... there's never anyone there.
Have you ever had a period in your life lasting at least a couple of weeks where you felt deeply down, depressed, or lost interest in things you usually enjoy?

Well, I wouldn't say I feel deeply depressed, exactly. It's more like... I just feel really flat. Like, I still care about people, but most days I just let texts sit unanswered. I skip hanging out after class. And even when my friends are talking about things I used to really enjoy, like music shows or art projects, I just... I don't feel anything about it. It's just flat.

Yeah, I have. There was actually a stretch of several weeks where... well, my mood was fine. I was sleeping normally, I didn't have that wound-up, intense energy at all. But I still heard the man's voice. And I still felt this... pull, I guess, into looking for patterns in the numbers at work. Even though everything else felt completely normal.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient demonstrates concurrent prominent affective (manic) and psychotic symptoms. Manic features include decreased need for sleep without fatigue, markedly elevated energy/unusual sharpness, irritability, and racing thoughts. Psychotic features include clear auditory hallucinations, disorganized thinking/formal thought disorder, and grossly disorganized or catatonic-like behavior. Crucially, the patient confirms experiencing auditory hallucinations and psychotic ideation for a stretch of several weeks in the absence of prominent mood symptoms, fulfilling the criteria for Schizoaffective disorder, manic type (ICD-10: F25.0).
